canonical_statement: The study investigates why entropy-based uncertainty estimation can become unreliable in retrieval-augmented generation and whether induction-head activity can be used to correct that failure mode.
Induction heads were identified using an induction score computed from attention to the correct historical offsets in a repeated random token sequence.
For hallucination analysis, the authors selected the five heads with the greatest induction scores and summarized their activity using SinkRate; larger SinkRate indicates weaker or absent induction.
Entropy neurons were operationalized in the final transformer block using the LogitVar score, and the mechanistic analyses focused on the 15 neurons with the lowest LogitVar scores.

Maximum-entropy score distributions for hallucinated and grounded responses overlapped heavily in the illustrated MS MARCO and XSum settings, supporting the authors’ claim that plain entropy is an unreliable RAG hallucination signal.
Mean SinkRate of the top-5 induction heads discriminated hallucinated from grounded MS MARCO responses generated by Llama-2-7B with AUROC 0.68.

canonical_statement: To test causality, correctly answered CoQA examples with SinkRate below the 0.33 quantile were subjected to mean ablation of the top-5 induction heads and compared with mean ablation of five randomly selected heads.

Mean ablation of induction heads increased negative log-likelihood and predictive entropy substantially more than ablation of random heads, which the authors interpret as causal evidence that induction heads support accurate context retrieval in RAG.
For Qwen3-8B and Llama-3.1-8B, most of the top-15 entropy neurons had negative Spearman correlation with SinkRate, linking stronger induction to greater entropy-neuron activation.
Mean ablation of the top-5 induction heads decreased the l2 norm of entropy-neuron activations, whereas the same pattern did not hold for randomly selected heads.
Mean ablation of the top-30 entropy neurons substantially decreased generation entropy, while ablation of 50 random neurons produced no significant change.

INTRYGUE computes token-level predictive entropy and multiplies an aggregated entropy score by an aggregated SinkRate score from the top-k induction heads, so high SinkRate amplifies uncertainty and low SinkRate dampens it.
The main experiments report two INTRYGUE variants: min-max aggregation uses minimum SinkRate and maximum token entropy, while mean aggregation averages both signals.
The evaluation covers four RAG tasks: MS MARCO long-form question answering and CNN/DailyMail summarization from RAGTruth, CoQA conversational question answering, and XSum extreme summarization.

population.label: Four RAG hallucination-detection benchmarks: MS MARCO, CNN/DM, CoQA, and XSum

canonical_statement: Six open-source models with accessible internal states were evaluated: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.1, Llama-2-7B-chat, Llama-2-13B-chat, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen3-8B, and Gemma-3-4B-it.
Gemma-3-4B-it, Llama-3.1-8B, and Qwen3-8B were evaluated only on CoQA and XSum because annotated RAGTruth responses were not available for those models.

The baseline set includes information-based uncertainty methods, sampling-diversity methods, and RAG-specific detectors including Lookback Lens, LUMINA, and ReDeEP; Lookback Lens was trained on the same data used for hyperparameter selection of the unsupervised methods.

canonical_statement: Applying nonlinear transformations such as Tanh or Softsign to the aggregated SinkRate did not provide significant benefit over using raw SinkRate values.
Average INTRYGUEmean AUROC remained stable when the number of induction heads k varied from 1 through 10, supporting the use of a fixed default such as k=5 without labeled validation data.
Across selected CoQA and MS MARCO model comparisons, INTRYGUEmin-max outperformed both minimum SinkRate and maximum entropy used in isolation.
A response-length-adaptive INTRYGUEdynamic variant matched or closely approached the stronger fixed aggregation in most reported model-dataset settings and sometimes exceeded both fixed variants.

canonical_statement: INTRYGUE requires white-box access to internal attention matrices and therefore cannot be directly applied to proprietary black-box models exposed only through APIs.
Because the method relies on standard Transformer attention mechanics, applicability to alternative architectures such as state-space models remains unresolved.

SinkRate is a proxy for induction-based context copying rather than a direct measurement of hallucination, so failures arising from unrelated mechanisms such as reasoning without context copying may not be isolated.
INTRYGUE estimates faithfulness to retrieved documents rather than objective factual truth; faithful use of false or conflicting retrieved content can therefore receive low uncertainty.

canonical_statement: Additional ablations varying the number of induction heads from top-1 to top-6 preserved the finding that induction-head ablation causes larger NLL and entropy shifts than random-head ablation.
Additional ablations varying the number of induction heads and ablating the top 10, 20, or 30 entropy neurons preserved the mechanistic trends reported in the main text.
All experiments used five random splits with seeds 42 through 46, train/validation/test fractions of 0.4/0.4/0.2, and NVIDIA L40 and H100 GPUs.
Sampling-based baselines used five additional model generations, except Semantic Density, which used ten additional generations.
The paper states that code is available through an anonymous link.
The authors state that the considered datasets contain no personally identifiable information or offensive content and were used according to their stated licenses.
The authors state that Gemini-3.1-Pro was used to proofread and refine the paper text for clarity.
A theoretical adversarial risk is that prompt injections could artificially increase induction-head activity and suppress the gated uncertainty score for manipulated outputs.

The authors conclude that RAG uncertainty estimation should combine predictive output uncertainty with internal evidence-utilization mechanisms, and that INTRYGUE provides a training-free way to do so by gating entropy with induction-head activity.
